label: Vent battery
detail: Warm alkaline vent fluid meets acidic ocean across thin iron-sulfur walls: a free ~200 mV battery.

label: Contact chemistry
detail: Reacts only to molecules that bump into its walls.

label: Diffusion
detail: Molecules wander. Crossing 1 µm takes ~0.5 ms; crossing 1 mm takes ~8 minutes.

label: Self-feeding chemistry
detail: Carbon fixation inside mineral pores, ~100 reactions per second per protocell.

label: Chemical levels
detail: About 100 bits of short-lived state per protocell.

label: Self-copying
detail: Whatever copies itself best persists.

label: RNA templates
detail: Ribozymes stuck to mineral surfaces: about 20,000 unique bits on the whole planet.

label: Pore clusters
detail: Thousands of mineral micro-compartments share one vent.

label: Ribosome
detail: A tape reader: reads three-letter codons and builds 15–20 amino acids per second.

label: Genetic code
detail: One codon table for nearly all life, with proofreading that catches most copying errors.

label: DNA genome
detail: Early cells carried millions of DNA letters, copied by proofreading enzymes with tiny error rates.

label: Gene swapping
detail: Early microbes swap genes sideways between neighbors, turning microbial communities into shared gene libraries.

label: Early photosynthesis
detail: Sunlight harvested with sulfur and iron, no oxygen released. Planet power: 0.44 TW.

label: Smell + swim
detail: Chemical sensors read the water; a spinning flagellum runs and tumbles.

label: Four-second memory
detail: Receptor tags compare the present with about 4 seconds ago.

label: Swim toward food
detail: Tumble less when things are getting better.

label: Partner microbes
detail: Different species trade waste for food.

label: Oxygen photosynthesis
detail: Splits water with sunlight and releases oxygen.

label: 24-hour clock
detail: A three-protein clock anticipates dawn. The planning horizon grows from 4 seconds to 24 hours.

label: Quorum sensing
detail: Microbial mats vote by chemical signal across up to ~10¹⁰ cells.

label: Breathing oxygen
detail: Burning sugar with oxygen yields 30–36 ATP instead of 2. Planet power: 3.5 TW.

label: Mitochondria
detail: An engulfed bacterium becomes a power plant: ~10,000× more energy per gene.

label: Molecular motors
detail: Kinesin and dynein walk cargo along polarized microtubule pipes at ~1–5 µm/s, beating diffusion inside big cells.

label: Complex-cell signaling
detail: Signal cascades and an internal skeleton, ~100,000 operations per second per cell.

label: Packed chromosomes
detail: DNA wound on protein spools lets genomes grow large.

label: Cells inside cells
detail: Two cells become one.

label: Chloroplast
detail: A swallowed cyanobacterium becomes a built-in solar panel.

label: Eyespot
detail: A light-sensitive spot steers two flagella within milliseconds.

label: Sex
detail: First fossil sexual life (Bangiomorpha, ~1.05 Ga): shuffling two genomes lets good mutations combine and bad ones get purged.

label: Many-celled bodies
detail: Clones stick together and split the work.

label: Synapse parts (spare)
detail: Proteins later used in synapses already exist, used for gluing cells together.

label: Fungal networks
detail: Fungal threads and colonial rosettes.

label: Chemical tissue waves
detail: Sponges coordinate pumping with nitric oxide and glutamate.

label: Bioelectric tissue
detail: Sheet-like bodies without synapses coordinate movement and feeding using peptides and voltage.

label: A front end
detail: Sensors cluster at the front of a two-sided body.

label: Bare nerve fibers
detail: Signals travel ~1 m/s; speed grows only with the square root of fiber width.

label: Neurons
detail: Nerve nets are in use by now: 10²⁰ synaptic events per second, planet-wide.

label: Firing patterns
detail: Spikes hold state for milliseconds to seconds.

label: Steering
detail: Approach good, avoid bad, in three dimensions. Bennett's Breakthrough 1.

label: Compound eyes
detail: Anomalocaris had more than 16,000 lenses per eye.

label: Three-part brain
detail: Early arthropods already had front, middle and rear brain parts with layered visual centers.

label: Distributed arm brains
detail: Cephalopod ancestors split computing between optic lobes and semi-independent arm cords.

label: Reef colonies
detail: Millions of coral and bryozoan clones share food and warning pulses across a living reef.

label: Learning from reward
detail: Dopamine signals surprise, so the brain learns from trial and error. Bennett's Breakthrough 2.

label: Synaptic memory
detail: Lessons from one lifetime get written into synapse strengths (~4–5 bits each).

label: Fish schools
detail: Early fish likely move as one, sensing neighbors in open water.

label: Water-ripple sense
detail: Hair cells and electric sensors along a fish's flank map unseen motion in murky water.

label: Split-second escape
detail: Giant command neurons flip a fish's tail within about 5 to 10 thousandths of a second of a threat.

label: Myelin
detail: Insulated fibers carry signals 50–100 m/s, at ~1% of the energy per centimeter.

label: Land plants
detail: Plants spread across the continents, and tall woody stems appear.

label: Wood-wide web
detail: Fungal threads link the roots of neighboring plants and trade nutrients.

label: Eyes in air
detail: Out of water, sight range grows ~100× and visible volume ~1,000,000×.

label: Look-ahead planning
detail: Seeing prey minutes away may reward weighing future paths.

label: Oxygen-rich air
detail: Oxygen surges toward ~30% and fuels giant flying insects.

label: Sparse insect brains
detail: Mushroom bodies fan smells across thousands of cells so a sparse handful tags each scent.

label: Three-layer forebrain
detail: Early land reptiles and synapsids build a three-layered forebrain that maps dry territories.

label: Shelled egg
detail: A waterproof egg carries its own pond and food supply, freeing land vertebrates from water.

label: Whiskers and scent scrolls
detail: Sensitive facial whiskers and scroll-shaped nose bones map the dark by touch and stereo smell.

label: Two-leg balance brain
detail: Fast inner-ear and cerebellar loops keep upright running dinosaurs balanced at speed.

label: Warm blood
detail: A 37 °C body keeps the brain fast, even at night.

label: Six-layer cortex
detail: The mammal cortex forms, wired to the hippocampus.

label: Mental maps
detail: Place cells hold where-am-I.

label: Imagining
detail: Replay rehearses paths not yet taken. Bennett's Breakthrough 3.

label: Three-bone ear
detail: Old jaw bones begin to become ear bones for high-pitched hearing.

label: Flight controller
detail: A bigger cerebellum and pallium steer in three dimensions.

label: Flocks and V-formations
detail: Birds likely flock by now; living starlings each track their seven nearest neighbors, passing turns across thousands with no leader.

label: Insect superorganisms
detail: Ants, bees and termites coordinate ~1,000,000 workers by scent and dance.

label: Family bonds
detail: Warm-blooded parents nurse, feed and call to their young, passing learned habits across generations.

label: Sharp forward-facing eyes
detail: Early primates bring both eyes forward for depth; three-color vision follows about 30 to 40 million years ago.

label: Folded neocortex
detail: By now monkeys' and apes' larger brains are folded, packing far more visual and social columns inside the skull.

label: Echolocation
detail: Toothed whales see with sound.

label: Dense bird brains
detail: Songbirds pack ~240 million neurons per gram.

label: Vocal pods and dialects
detail: Whale pods and songbirds learn family dialects, coordinating hunts and territories over kilometers.

label: Reading minds
detail: A prefrontal cortex models what others know. Bennett's Breakthrough 4.

label: Troops and coalitions
detail: Apes and monkeys track allies and rivals in groups of ~50–80 through grooming and alarm calls.

label: Upright walking
detail: Balancing on two legs frees the hands from walking so fingers can carry, gesture and build.

label: Matriarch clans
detail: Long-lived elders lead nested elephant and savanna herds via low rumbles and ground vibrations.

label: Tool-using hands
detail: Striking stone extends what hands can do.

label: Stone tools
detail: The first memory outside a body: a knapped stone keeps a plan for 10,000+ years at zero watts.

label: Hand-eye tool circuits
detail: Expanded parietal-premotor loops aim stone strikes at exact angles as hominin brains jump 50%.

label: Fire and cooking
detail: Possibly tending fire already; cooking digests food outside the body, freeing energy for a bigger brain.

label: Multi-step tool plans
detail: Modern-sized brains hold nested sub-goals to shape stone cores and hafted wooden spears.

label: Cooperative bands
detail: Hominin families share childcare across grandparents and coordinate team hunts of big game.

label: Engraved symbols
detail: Ochre plaques and shell beads carry meaning.

label: Speech
detail: About 39 bits per second, across all 17 languages measured.

label: Language
detail: By now nested grammar moves plans and stories between minds. Bennett's Breakthrough 5.

label: Cave art and tallies
detail: Painted walls and notched bones store stories and counts outside the head.

label: Tribes
detail: Groups of ~1,500 bound by a shared language.

label: Farming
detail: Crops and herds turn sunlight into a dependable surplus.

label: Villages
detail: Settled villages of 500–2,000 people.

label: Clay tokens
detail: Counters sealed inside hollow clay balls get pressed into the surface, turning objects into signs.

label: Clay writing
detail: Baked clay tablets last thousands of years with no power.

label: City-states
detail: Uruk: ~50,000 people coordinated by written ledgers.

label: Alphabet
detail: About 22 letters replace thousands of signs (~5 bits per letter).

label: Formal logic and grammar
detail: Panini's ~4,000 grammar rules and Greek step-by-step proofs turn reasoning into written rules.

label: Coins and markets
detail: Stamped metal coins put a shared number on value, coordinating trade across strangers.

label: Gear computer
detail: The Antikythera mechanism predicts the sky with bronze gears.

label: Empires
detail: Over the next three centuries Rome and Han China each come to govern ~60 million people.

label: The book
detail: Pages replace scrolls: jump straight to any passage.

label: Zero and algorithms
detail: Place-value numbers with zero turn hard arithmetic into step-by-step recipes on paper.

label: Rag-paper mills
detail: Water-powered mills turn linen rags into affordable sheets, multiplying books before print.

label: Printing press
detail: Copying cost falls ~300×; ~20 million books in 50 years.

label: Mechanical calculators
detail: Pascal and Leibniz build adding machines.

label: Scientific journals
detail: Public journals launch checkable, shared scientific memory across countries.

label: Coal and steam
detail: Coal-fired steam engines push human power use past 0.85 TW.

label: Telegraph
detail: Signals cross continents at ~70% of light speed, two million times faster than a nerve.

label: Punch-card machines
detail: Hollerith's machines count the 1890 US census.

label: Electronic computers
detail: ENIAC and EDVAC: ~100,000 operations per second worldwide.

label: Stored programs
detail: Instructions live in memory as data, so machines can be reprogrammed.

label: Microchips
detail: Many transistors on one silicon chip; Moore's law begins.

label: Electronic memory
detail: Magnetic cores, then DRAM, hold a running program's state.

label: ARPANET
detail: Computers start talking to each other in packets.

label: Fiber optics
detail: Light in glass carries the web.

label: Digital storage
detail: Digital storage nears and soon passes all paper, film and vinyl combined.

label: World Wide Web
detail: Nearly 400 million people go online across a world of 6.1 billion, linked to ~1 billion chips.

label: GPUs that learn
detail: Graphics chips get repurposed to train neural networks.

label: Transformers
detail: One AI architecture for language, code and proteins.

label: 84.5 TW
detail: Living cells and animals burn ~65 TW to stay alive (a bottom-up estimate); human technology adds 19.5 TW.

label: AI supercomputers
detail: One cluster runs 3×10²⁰ operations per second.

label: Memory everywhere
detail: Refreshed every 64 ms; refreshing alone uses ~11 GW worldwide.

label: Machines that deliberate
detail: Models think step by step before answering.

label: 15 zettabytes
detail: 1.2×10²³ bits stored, kept alive by ~20 GW of power.

label: Planetary network
detail: 8.1 billion people and 6.5 billion devices.

label: Template copying
detail: Mineral-held RNA chains catalyse rough copies of neighbors before cells exist.

label: Cell division
detail: One cell copies its DNA tape and ribosomes, then pinches into two complete cells.

label: Coordinated mitosis
detail: Host nucleus and engulfed mitochondria synchronize their division on protein spindles.

label: Single-cell bottleneck
detail: Many-celled bodies reset to one fertilized egg or spore so every body builds fresh.

label: Body-plan toolkit
detail: Shared Hox master switches stamp out modular segments, limbs and sense organs.

label: Spores and seeds
detail: Dormant plant embryos travel overland with packed food, germinating years later.

label: Metamorphosis
detail: One insect genome builds a feeding larva first and rebuilds it into a winged adult.

label: Reproductive castes
detail: One queen lays millions of eggs while sterile worker castes forage and build as one body.

label: Live birth and milk
detail: Warm internal gestation and nursing grow slow-wiring brains safely beside a parent.

label: Stone toolmaking
detail: Hands shape raw cobbles into repeatable cutting edges passed down by watching.

label: Domestication
detail: Farmers steer the reproduction of wheat, rice, sheep and cattle for bigger harvests.

label: Interchangeable type
detail: A hand mold casts thousands of identical metal letters, launching mass manufacture.

label: Factories and lathes
detail: Steam-powered lathes and looms cut interchangeable parts that build more machines.

label: Chip photolithography
detail: Light projects circuit masks onto silicon wafers, printing millions of switches at once.

label: EUV fabs and gene writing
detail: Ultraviolet fabs print 100-billion-transistor chips while DNA printers write custom genes.

label: AI-designed chips and proteins
detail: Models co-design chip floorplans, robot code and proteins, though fabs still need humans.

label: Organelle gene transfer
detail: Mitochondria and chloroplasts move thousands of genes into the nucleus, keeping tiny local genomes beside their membranes.

label: Two genome doublings
detail: Early vertebrates copy their entire genome twice, freeing spare genes to wire new brains, jaws and senses.

label: Plant & fish polyploidy
detail: Seed plants and bony fish double whole genomes again, fueling vast radiations on land and in water.

label: Lean dinosaur genomes
detail: Two-legged dinosaurs shed repeated DNA for smaller cells and high-speed oxygen use long before birds fly.

label: Flowers and pollinators
detail: Repeated genome doublings build flowers, nectar and double fertilization, recruiting insects and birds as flying pollen couriers.

label: Our 3.1B-letter genome
detail: Humans carry ~20,000 protein genes plus vast regulatory switches; each child inherits ~70 new DNA letter changes.

label: Reading DNA
detail: Sequencers read viral, bacterial and soon human genomes letter by letter, turning heredity into digital text.

label: CRISPR & synthetic DNA
detail: Chemically written genomes boot living cells, CRISPR cuts chosen DNA letters, and books are stored in DNA.

label: 3.6×10³⁷ DNA bits
detail: Split roughly evenly between microbes and complex cells; ferns hold 160B letters while Paramecium errs 1 in 50B.

label: Meiotic toolkit
detail: Early complex cells repurpose DNA-repair enzymes to pair chromosomes, swap segments and halve gene copies.

label: Mating types
detail: Single-celled algae evolve plus and minus surface tags so stressed cells fuse only with an opposite partner.

label: Sperm and egg
detail: Equal gametes split jobs into millions of tiny swimming sperm that search and large food-packed eggs that build embryos.

label: Synchronized spawning
detail: Early sea animals release clouds of eggs and scent-guided sperm in lockstep with moonlight and chemical cues.

label: Internal fertilization
detail: Jawed armored fish evolve claspers for direct mating instead of open-water clouds, setting up reproduction on land.

label: Pollen & land mating
detail: Seed plants pipe sperm through tiny pollen tubes while early reptiles pair on land to lay waterproof shelled eggs.

label: XY & ZW chromosomes
detail: Mammals and birds lock sex onto dedicated chromosomes instead of nest temperature, stabilizing 50:50 sex ratios.

label: Courtship & mate choice
detail: Learned birdsong, whale songs and bright displays turn mate choice into an engine of sensory and brain evolution.

label: Pair bonds & grandmothers
detail: Long pair bonds, shared family care and post-menopausal grandmothers pool food so slow-growing human brains mature.

label: IVF & embryo screening
detail: In-vitro fertilization, cryopreservation and genetic screening let medicine assist conception and check embryos.

label: Spaceflight guidance
detail: Apollo's 72-kilobyte microchip computer lands humans on the Moon 384,400 km away, shedding radar overloads mid-descent.

label: Deep-space probes
detail: Plutonium-powered Voyagers carry six radiation-hardened computers and billion-year gold records past the outer planets into interstellar space.

label: Autonomous rovers
detail: With radio taking 4–24 minutes to reach Mars, radiation-hardened rovers dodge hazards and pick laser targets on their own.

label: Deep-space & orbital lasers
detail: 70-meter dishes catch 160-bit/s whispers from interstellar space while infrared lasers wire satellites and deep-space probes.

label: Off-world fleet (1 light-day)
detail: ~17,500 active satellites, L2 telescopes, Mars robots and Voyager 1 at 25.9 billion km extend Earth's senses into the stars.

label: CRISPR viral memory
detail: Bacteria snip DNA from attacking viruses and file it in their own genome as a mugshot gallery for next time.

label: Adaptive immunity
detail: Jawed fish shuffle antibody gene segments into billions of detectors, keeping lifetime memory of past germs.

label: Plant calcium memory
detail: Land plants count touches over 20 seconds with calcium pulses and remember winter cold in chromatin marks.

label: Plant warning waves
detail: Bitten leaves fire glutamate-calcium waves down stems and release scents that prime neighboring leaves.

label: Prefrontal working memory
detail: Primate frontal loops hold active goals and rules online across distractions so plans survive interruptions.

label: Counting boards & abacus
detail: Pebbles and sliding beads hold intermediate sums outside the skull, breaking our ~4-item mental scratchpad limit.

label: Pocket smartphone sensors
detail: Over a billion phones pair cameras, microphones and GPS with mobile networks, sensing the live planet.

label: Synthetic bacterial cell
detail: Chemists stitch 1.08 million DNA letters from a computer file to boot the first living cell with a human-written genome.

label: Attention context cache
detail: Transformer key-value caches keep hundreds of thousands of words live in fast chip memory while reasoning.

label: Programmable mRNA vaccines
detail: Digitally written messenger RNA in lipid droplets teaches human cells to print viral proteins and build immunity.

label: Pinhole & jellyfish lens eyes
detail: Pigment cups deepen into Nautilus-style pinholes and 24-eye box-jellyfish clusters with graded lenses, turning shadows into true directions.

label: Crystal & mirror eyes
detail: Trilobites grind aberration-free doublet lenses from pure calcite crystal while scallops focus light off 200 curved guanine mirrors.

label: 16-color & polarized eyes
detail: Reef mantis shrimp split UV-to-red light across up to 16 opsin channels plus circular polarization, spotting signals invisible to fish.

label: 28,000-facet 300-Hz eyes
detail: Giant aerial hunters wrap nearly 360 degrees of sky in 28,000 facets, refreshing motion up to 300 times a second to intercept prey mid-air.

label: Rod-packed night retina
detail: Nocturnal early mammals trade two color cones for 100 million single-photon rods and an eye-shine mirror, spanning ten billion-fold light levels.

label: Four-color & eagle fovea
detail: Feathered dinosaurs and birds keep UV-plus-RGB cones filtered by colored oil droplets, reaching 140 cycles per degree in eagles.

label: Three-color primate fovea
detail: Old World monkeys duplicate a green-red opsin gene, lighting up ripe fruit and social blushes against green leaves at 60 cycles per degree.

label: 8-kg whale & dolphin brains
detail: Sperm whales and dolphins grow the heaviest brains in Earth's history (up to 7.8 kg and 37B neurons), wiring sonar and lifetime clan dialects.

label: 69B-neuron cerebellum
detail: Four-fifths of human brain neurons pack into cerebellar forward-timing models, smoothing rapid stone-knapping, balance and later speech.

label: 100:1 retinal edge filter
detail: Five layers of human retinal neurons distil 126 million receptors into ~30 parallel edge and motion movies before a spike enters the brain.

label: Arcuate language highway
detail: An expanded white-matter arch links auditory, conceptual and motor cortex across 180 areas so humans parse nested speech at 39 bits per second.

label: CMOS & neuromorphic cameras
detail: Stacked 200-megapixel CMOS sensors, microsecond event retinas and bionic subretinal chips give machines and medicine synthetic sight.
